label: hemianatropous
definition: An orientation quality inhering in an ovule by virtue of its body being turned through about a right angle on its funicle, so that the micropyle points sideways and the funicle is attached near the middle of one side. NOTE: Botany-specific; PATO has none of the ovule orientations (anatropous, orthotropous, campylotropous), which should follow as siblings.
reason: A standard ovule type with no PATO or FLOPO term; it is an orientation of the ovule body relative to its funicle.
PO has no raphide cell; the absence of the broader idioblast (PO_0000283) would overstate the statement. A specialist anatomical character.

A crown narrow at the base and widening upward to a spreading top, like a shuttlecock, is obconical; only two statements.
Two values run together: cylindrical (PATO_0001873) and slender (narrow in diameter); the bearer is spadix appendix (FLOPO_0986049).
'Arising at a steep angle' is the angle of a vein to the midvein from which it arises, a relation to another part, not a quality of the vein alone.

label: obtetrahedral
definition: A convex 3-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being shaped like a tetrahedron attached at one of its angles, so that a broad triangular face is distal. NOTE: PATO has no tetrahedral shape; follows the inverted shapes FLOPO:0991185 obtriangular and FLOPO:0991025 obovoid.
reason: A clear solid shape of fruits with no existing term.
PATO_0002215 falciform has the synonyms hooked, uncinate and unciform.
Seed surface combining spines and thin plates: two surface values run together, not one quality.

label: obliquely truncate
definition: A truncated quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's apex or orifice ending abruptly in a straight edge that is oblique to the bearer's long axis. NOTE: Child of PATO:0000936 truncated; used of the orifice of the perigynium beak in Carex.
reason: A standard Carex character (91 statements) with no term; PATO_0002481 oblique orientation is the direction of a whole part, not the cut of its apex.
